processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene as process control reagent (to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent process (proc_ma-35h). Starting elemental powder Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C (99.2% pure) in Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 proportion; planetary ball mill Retsch PM 400/2 at 200 rpm, ball-to-powder ratio 10:1, tungsten carbide (WC) vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating. This 35 h milled powder is the starting material for the 500 °C anneal.

processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (35 h milled powder encapsulated in a quartz tube back-filled with argon)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 35 h milled powder was annealed for 1 h at 500 °C (one of 400, 500, 600 and 800 °C conditions) followed by water quenching, to study thermal stability. ~500 °C is the upper bound of thermal stability of the milled powder.

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase structure retained at 500 °C: BCC (major phase) + γ-brass type + partially ordered B2-type, with a trace amount of undissolved Si. The metastable milled alloy remains thermally stable at 500 °C; no Fe5Si3-type silicide is formed (it appears only from 600 °C onward).

phases_present.crystal_structure: cI2 (BCC); a = 0.286 nm; unit cell volume 23.39 Å³
cI52 (γ-brass type); a = 0.872 nm; unit cell volume 663.05 Å³
cP2 (partially ordered B2); a = 0.289 nm; unit cell volume 24.13 Å³

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku X-ray diffractometer, Cu-Kα source, 40 kV, 15 mA, scan rate 5° min⁻¹
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Ex-situ XRD of 35 h milled powders annealed at 400, 500, 600 and 800 °C; 2θ range 20-100°, with enlarged 2θ = 42°-46° region and deconvolution around the BCC (110) peak
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the phase evolution/thermal stability of the 35 h milled powder upon annealing
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 500 °C the phases remain BCC + γ-brass type + B2-type (deconvolution of the (110) region resolves BCC, B2 and γ-brass components); the Fe5Si3-type silicide is absent at 500 °C and only appears at 600 °C.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Chebyschev-I background function with 10 coefficients; pseudo-Voigt profile function (Lorentzian + Gaussian broadening); uniaxial model for crystallite size and isotropic microstrain
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase fraction, lattice parameter and crystallite size of the annealed samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: 500 °C: BCC 47.70%, γ-brass type 36.30%, B2 16.00%; lattice parameters BCC 0.286 nm, γ-brass type 0.872 nm, B2 0.289 nm; crystallite sizes BCC 23 nm, γ-brass type 16 nm, B2 20 nm; fit quality wR = 2.279, GoF = 1.04, χ² = 1.07.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Netzsch DSC404 Pegasus differential scanning calorimeter
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 35 h milled powder heated up to 1000 °C at 20 K/min under nitrogen (N2) atmosphere
characterization_methods.purpose: Study the thermal stability of the milled powder and locate exothermic events that guided the annealing temperatures
characterization_methods.key_findings: Exothermic events at ~420 °C (693 K) attributed to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase and at ~520 °C (793 K) attributed to Fe5Si3-type silicide formation; the 500 °C annealing condition lies below the 520 °C silicide event.

computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic modelling (property diagram and single-point equilibrium calculation)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pressure = 100000.0 Pa; system size = 1.0 mol; mole fraction Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.10, C = 0.01 (balance Fe). Single-point equilibrium at 1200, 1100, 800, 500 and 300 °C — at 500 °C (773 K) predicted phases: BCC_A2#1 = 0.69, B2 = 0.28, BCC_A2#2 = 0.02, M3Si = 0.01 mol.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: CALPHAD-predicted phases (BCC, partially ordered B2, γ-brass type) were correlated with the experimentally observed phases of the annealed/SPSed samples; differences between prediction and experiment are attributed to use of the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3.

unmapped_findings: The 35 h milled powder is thermally stable up to ~500 °C; at the 500 °C annealing condition the phases BCC + γ-brass type + B2-type are retained and no Fe5Si3-type silicide is formed (the silicide appears only from 600 °C onward).

DTA of the 35 h milled powder shows two exothermic events, at ~420 °C (693 K) assigned to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase and at ~520 °C (793 K) assigned to the formation of the Fe5Si3-type phase; the 500 °C annealing temperature is below the 520 °C silicide-formation event.
Rietveld refinement quality for the 500 °C annealed sample: wR = 2.279, GoF = 1.04, χ² = 1.07.

Room-temperature phase assemblage of the milled/annealed alloy is reported as BCC + γ-brass type + B2 + Si (undissolved). At 500 °C the γ-brass type phase fraction increased relative to the as-milled powder, and some new peaks evolved (Fig. 5 deconvolution around the BCC (110) peak).

No mechanical/physical property measurements (microhardness, elastic modulus, compressive strength, density) were performed on the 500 °C annealed powder; the reported values 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa microhardness, 184 ± 5 GPa elastic modulus and 2046 ± 160 MPa compressive strength with ~19% ductility belong to the SPSed sample, not to this annealed-powder sample.
